workouts.title: Aerobic Base Run + Hill Sprints
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy running in Zone 1 (7:00/km) → Steady aerobic running 75 min in Zone 2 on rolling terrain (6:10/km) → 6 x 10s maximum uphill sprints on steep 15% grade, each with 3 min full walking/standing recovery → Cool down 10 min easy jog (7:15/km). Overall: Sustained aerobic volume run on rolling trail terrain followed by explosive neuromuscular hill sprints. This introduces week 1 running volume while maintaining pure aerobic metabolism below AeT. The short hill sprints engage high-threshold motor units without accumulating metabolic fatigue. Reason: Establishes aerobic baseline volume following the athlete's high weekly running history and primes high-threshold neuromuscular recruitment early in the 10-week runway. Benefit: Enhances mitochondrial density and capillarization in slow-twitch fibers while recruiting fast-twitch motor units without glycolytic acidosis. Warning: Hill sprints must be performed with complete 3-minute recoveries to ensure ATP replenishment; terminate sprints immediately if mechanical power drops or hamstring tightness occurs.

workouts.title: Mountain Long Run + Power Hiking
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min progressive trail jogging from Zone 1 to Zone 2 → Continuous trail endurance 150 min in Zone 2 alternating running on flats and descents with deliberate power-hiking on sustained steep climbs over 12% grade, using trekking poles → Cool down 15 min flat easy walking and jog recovery. Overall: Mountain-specific aerobic long run incorporating high vertical climbing to prepare for the extreme 52.5 m D+/km course profile. Heart rate is kept strictly below AeT (133 bpm) at all times, transitioning to power hiking as soon as grade spikes to prevent crossing AnT. Reason: Specific endurance simulation to condition eccentric knee extensor tolerance and develop fatigue-resistant movement economy on mountain gradients. Benefit: Expands aerobic fat-oxidation rates, conditions patellar and Achilles tendons to repetitive mountain impact, and refines uphill power-hiking economy. Warning: Strictly monitor heart rate on sustained ascents to prevent drifting above AeT (133 bpm); hike early on steep inclines to protect muscular longevity.

workouts.title: Aerobic Base Volume + Muscular Endurance Circuit
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy running @ Zone 1-2 → 20 reps Bodyweight Air Squats, 15s transition → 10 reps per leg Reverse Lunges, 15s transition → 10 reps per leg Eccentric Step-Downs off 30cm curb or rock, 15s transition → 15 reps Single-Leg Calf Raises per leg, 60s rest → Repeat circuit for 4 total rounds (20 min total) → Cool down 50 min continuous aerobic trail/road running @ Zone 2. Overall: Combined aerobic base run and bodyweight muscular endurance circuit designed to build local leg stamina and eccentric resilience. Initiates the specific Muscular Endurance block required by the 10-week compressed runway without gym equipment. Keeps cardiac demand low while accumulating necessary peripheral adaptation. Reason: Scheduled on Monday following a rest day to establish early weekly volume and introduce local neuromuscular fatigue resistance while fresh. Benefit: Improves recruitment of slow-twitch and intermediate fast-twitch motor units without cardiac strain, strengthening connective tissue against downhill degradation. Warning: Maintain strictly conversational breathing during the circuit; terminate reps immediately if form breaks down or knee tracking wobbles.

workouts.title: Aerobic Base Run + Steep Hill Sprints
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 65 min continuous aerobic running @ Zone 2 (120-133 bpm) → 8 x 10s maximum-effort steep hill sprints on a 10-15% grade with 3 min standing or slow walking recovery between reps (25 min total) → Cool down 10 min easy jog @ Zone 1. Overall: Substantial aerobic volume run incorporating neuromuscular alactic hill sprints to recruit high-threshold motor units. Hill sprints provide explosive power and running economy improvements without inducing metabolic acidosis. Prepares neuromuscular pathways for extreme mountain vert. Reason: Positioned early in the training week to train neuromuscular recruitment before cumulative fatigue sets in, while continuing high base accumulation. Benefit: Enhances motor unit recruitment, tendon stiffness, and mechanical efficiency while keeping overall cardiovascular strain strictly aerobic. Warning: Hill sprints must be absolute maximum effort but strictly 10 seconds; full 3-minute passive recoveries are mandatory to replenish phosphocreatine stores completely.

workouts.title: Scheduled Rest & Regeneration
workouts.description: Process: Complete full rest day → Light mobility and tissue work for 15-20 min if desired → Hydrate and focus on nutrient-dense meals. Overall: Dedicated mid-week rest day to absorb early-week training stress and allow complete muscular repair. Rest days are essential to consolidate neuromuscular adaptations from hill sprints and muscular endurance work. Keeps systemic fatigue low for the high-volume days ahead. Reason: Aligned with the athlete's preferred off-day schedule and Uphill Athlete principles of deliberate recovery. Benefit: Facilitates muscle protein synthesis, glycogen supercompensation, and autonomic nervous system replenishment. Warning: Avoid strenuous cross-training, prolonged standing, or unprescribed heavy yard work.

workouts.title: Aerobic Base Endurance Run
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min progressive jog from Zone 1 to Zone 2 → 90 min continuous steady aerobic running on rolling terrain holding Zone 2 heart rate strictly below 133 bpm → Cool down 10 min easy walking and light stretching. Overall: Extended mid-week aerobic endurance run to accumulate volume and stimulate fat metabolism. Rolling hills provide natural changes in cadence and hip extension while respecting aerobic thresholds. Directly develops capillary beds and mitochondrial density in slow-twitch fibers. Reason: Critical volume day to maintain the targeted 130-140 km/week baseline load without crossing into high-fatigue threshold zones. Benefit: Expands aerobic enzymatic capacity, strengthens joint complexes, and optimizes lipid oxidation efficiency for ultra distances. Warning: Keep heart rate strictly below the 133 bpm AeT ceiling on all uphill portions; transition to a brisk hike if heart rate approaches 133 bpm.

workouts.title: Aerobic Recovery & Foundation Run
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy gentle jogging @ Zone 1 → 70 min steady, relaxed low-intensity running @ Zone 1-2 (strictly 110-125 bpm) → Cool down 10 min walking and mobility. Overall: Low-intensity base run focused on active recovery and aerobic volume accumulation. Maintains blood flow to working muscles to flush metabolic waste ahead of the demanding weekend. Ensures structural loading remains sustainable at sub-elite volume levels. Reason: Prepares the muscular and energetic systems for the heavy weekend volume block without adding global cardiovascular fatigue. Benefit: Enhances venous return, promotes soft tissue remodeling, and reinforces fat oxidation mechanics without nervous system tax. Warning: Strictly avoid running into high Zone 2 or Zone 3; if legs feel heavy, slow down to a recovery shuffle.

workouts.title: Mountain Vert Simulation & Sub-Threshold Repeats
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 25 min easy trail running @ Zone 1-2 → 3 x 15 min steady uphill tempo climbing @ Zone 3 (135-152 bpm, below AnT 162 bpm), 5 min easy jog descent recovery between reps (55 min total) → 45 min steady rolling aerobic trail running @ Zone 2 → Cool down 10 min walking and stretching. Overall: Sub-threshold mountain session targeting sustained uphill climbing power without exceeding anaerobic threshold. The continuous climbing efforts develop lactate shuttle capacity and quad fatigue resistance on substantial vertical gain. Keeps global systemic fatigue manageable while driving race-specific power. Reason: First half of the back-to-back weekend mountain block, capitalizing on rested weekend schedule to simulate course steepness. Benefit: Improves sustainable uphill climbing velocity, local muscular endurance in hip extensors, and aerobic power at sub-threshold intensities. Warning: Keep intensity strictly capped below 155 bpm to avoid producing excess lactate that would impair Sunday's long run.

workouts.title: Mountain Long Run + Power Hiking Endurance
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy hiking and slow jog @ Zone 1 → 200 min steady mountain trail running and aggressive uphill power hiking on steep climbs @ Zone 1-2 (strictly capping HR at 133 bpm on all ascents, practicing controlled technical descents) → Cool down 15 min easy flat walking and mobility. Overall: Specific mountain ultra simulation run focusing on vertical accumulation, sustained aerobic output, and gut training under fatigue. Incorporates technical descents to condition quads eccentrically for the extreme 52.5 m D+/km race profile. Teaches disciplined energy conservation and pacing over multiple hours of mountain movement. Reason: Culmination of the weekly training stimulus, completing the back-to-back weekend mountain block within the 30% weekly volume limit. Benefit: Stimulates profound mitochondrial density, capillary growth, fat oxidation, and eccentric tendon/fascia resilience required for technical 80K ultra racing. Warning: Never run the steep uphill grades; enforce disciplined power-hiking with poles whenever the trail exceeds 10% to prevent spiking heart rate into Zone 3/4.

workouts.title: Aerobic Base Trail Run & Neuromuscular Hill Sprints
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy continuous running @ Zone 1-2 → 75 min steady mountain trail running @ Zone 2 heart rate strictly below 133 bpm → 6 x 10s steep hill sprints @ Zone 5 maximal sprint effort on a 15% grade, 3 min standing recovery between reps → Cool down 12 min easy jogging @ Zone 1. Overall: An aerobic base trail volume session incorporating steep neuromuscular hill sprints near the end. This stimulates high-threshold motor unit recruitment without cardiac or systemic glycolytic fatigue. Reason: Scheduled on the opening Saturday of this abbreviated 10-week runway to establish aerobic baseline volume and recruit fast-twitch muscle fibers via neuromuscular hill sprints. Benefit: Increases mitochondrial enzyme density, enhances running economy, and stimulates full motor unit recruitment without triggering cardiovascular fatigue. Warning: Hill sprint repetitions must strictly be capped at 10-12 seconds with full 3-minute passive recoveries; if form deteriorates or power drops, terminate sprints immediately to avoid hamstring strain.

workouts.title: Mountain Specific Long Run & Technical Vert
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy progressive jog @ Zone 1 → 95 min aerobic trail mountain run and power-hiking sustained climbs @ Zone 2 strictly below 133 bpm → Cool down 15 min easy jog on gradual decline @ Zone 1. Overall: A high-vert mountain long run simulating the sustained gradients and technical footwork required for extreme vertical trail racing. Maintains strict Zone 2 metabolic parameters to build specific fatigue resistance. Reason: Positioned on Sunday to respect preferred scheduling and build aerobic endurance on mountainous terrain while honoring the athlete's proven single-run distance volume ceiling. Benefit: Expands capillary density, improves fatty acid oxidation at race pace, and triggers eccentric muscular conditioning across the quadriceps and connective tissues. Warning: Monitor heart rate vigilantly on steep technical ascents; switch immediately to power-hiking with poles whenever heart rate approaches 133 bpm to avoid entering Zone 3.

workouts.title: Short Runway Muscular Endurance Bodyweight Circuit
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 10 min dynamic mobility and ankle activation → 10 reps Split Jump Squats, 15s transition → 10 reps Squat Jumps, 15s transition → 10 reps per leg Box Step-Ups at kneecap height, 15s transition → 10 reps per leg Front Lunges, 15s transition → 6 rounds total with 60s rest between rounds → Cool down 5 min gentle lower-body mobility and stretching. Overall: A sport-specific bodyweight muscular endurance circuit executed as an afternoon session to initiate localized peripheral muscular fatigue resistance without gym weights. Reason: Under the short 10-week runway override rule, specific muscular endurance circuits begin in Week 1 to prepare the athlete's legs for 4,200m of mountain vertical. Benefit: Increases muscular buffering capacity and recruits Type IIa frontier muscle fibers under localized tension without creating high cardiac load. Warning: Maintain flawless knee-over-toe tracking on all jump landings; if technique breaks down or landing becomes heavy, pause the circuit to protect patellar tendons.

workouts.title: Aerobic Base Trail Run & Neuromuscular Hill Sprints
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 20 min easy trail running @ 5:10/km, Zone 1 → 60 min steady aerobic trail running @ 4:40/km, Zone 2 → 8 x 12s hill sprints @ Zone 5 max effort on 15% grade, 3 min standing recovery → Cool down 15 min easy jog @ 5:15/km, Zone 1. Overall: An aerobic base accumulation trail run combined with explosive steep hill sprints to develop maximal neuromuscular recruitment without metabolic fatigue. This anchors the aerobic week while preserving fast-twitch fiber activation for mountain running. Maintain strict nasal breathing and conversational effort during the aerobic segments. Reason: Placed on Monday to establish weekly aerobic consistency and fire up motor units via pure alactic hill sprints after previous missed logs. Benefit: Expands capillary density, elevates cardiac stroke volume, and recruits high-threshold FTa motor units with zero systemic lactate accumulation. Warning: Ensure complete 3-minute passive recovery between hill sprints; do not begin a rep while breathing hard or feeling residual leg pump.

workouts.title: Sub-Threshold Steady State & Mountain Aerobic Volume
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 20 min easy @ 4:55/km, Zone 1-2 → 2 x 25 min steady mountain tempo @ 4:15/km, Zone 3 below AnT, 5 min easy jog recovery between sets → 10 min easy Zone 2 running @ 4:45/km → Cool down 15 min easy @ 5:10/km, Zone 1. Overall: A controlled sub-threshold Zone 3 continuous stimulus designed to expand oxidative capacity on rolling mountain grades without inducing high systemic fatigue. Zone 3 work remains comfortably below AnT to minimize autonomic nervous system stress. Keeps total intensity strictly contained while building heavy sustained climbing endurance. Reason: Provides a robust aerobic overload session early in the microcycle with low global fatigue cost prior to Wednesday's scheduled rest. Benefit: Enhances lactate clearance, upregulates mitochondrial density in slow-twitch fibers, and conditions legs to continuous moderate mountain rhythm. Warning: Strictly cap heart rate below 155 bpm on all uphill pitches; do not drift into Zone 4 threshold territory.

workouts.title: Full Rest & Tissue Regeneration
workouts.description: Process: Full complete rest day with zero running impact → 15 min gentle mobility and hip flow. Overall: Scheduled weekly rest day to absorb early-week volume and prepare the neuromuscular system for back-to-back training blocks. Complete downtime permits soft tissue remodeling, tendon restoration, and full glycogen resynthesis. Prioritize deep rest, balanced nutrition, and hydration. Reason: Scheduled on athlete's designated non-training day to consolidate training adaptations and avoid structural overload. Benefit: Facilitates systemic endocrine recovery, clears accumulated metabolic byproducts, and maintains long-term structural integrity. Warning: Avoid strenuous cross-training, high-intensity domestic labor, or prolonged standing that interferes with physiological supercompensation.

workouts.title: Short Runway Muscular Endurance Bodyweight Circuit
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 10 min dynamic mobility and light joint prep → 10 reps Split Jump Squats, 15s transition → 10 reps Squat Jumps, 15s transition → 10 reps per leg Box Step-Ups at kneecap height, 15s transition → 10 reps per leg Walking Lunges → Repeat circuit for 6 total rounds with 60s rest between rounds → Cool down 5 min gentle walking and leg stretching. Overall: A high-rep bodyweight muscular endurance circuit executed strictly under the Scott Johnston framework to build localized peripheral resistance against uphill fatigue. Cardiovascular demand stays low while intermediate muscle fibers develop superior fatigue resistance. Essential for extreme technical mountain vert where local muscular failure governs pace. Reason: Bypasses standard barbell strength to establish early mountain muscular endurance on an abbreviated 10-week runway without gym equipment. Benefit: Increases intramuscular glycogen storage, enhances local buffering capacity, and shields quadriceps from downhill eccentric damage. Warning: Maintain flawless knee and pelvic alignment throughout all jump landings; terminate rep if form breaks or landing becomes heavy.

workouts.title: Aerobic Base Trail Run & Strides
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy trail running @ 5:10/km, Zone 1 → 60 min steady aerobic running @ 4:40/km, Zone 2 → 5 x 20s relaxed strides on flat trail @ Zone 4 pace, 60s walk recovery → Cool down 10 min easy jog @ 5:15/km, Zone 1. Overall: A steady aerobic base trail run dedicated to accumulating low-fatigue aerobic volume and reinforcing clean biomechanics. The brief strides at the end promote hip extension and turnover without generating cardiovascular fatigue. Keeps the aerobic system primed ahead of the substantial weekend mountain volume. Reason: Bridges the Thursday muscular endurance circuit and the weekend long endurance blocks while protecting aerobic development. Benefit: Promotes lipid metabolism, increases mitochondrial enzymes, and reinforces economical stride mechanics. Warning: Keep the strides relaxed and flowing rather than strained or all-out sprints; focus on posture and arm carriage.

workouts.title: Aerobic Base Trail Volume & Grade Progression
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy @ 5:10/km, Zone 1 → 85 min continuous aerobic trail running across varied technical grades @ 4:40/km, Zone 2 → Cool down 15 min easy jog @ 5:15/km, Zone 1. Overall: A substantial aerobic endurance run on hilly trails designed to simulate multi-hour climbing demands while strictly guarding aerobic threshold discipline. Power-hike steep sections as necessary to keep heart rate firmly under AeT. Forms the first leg of back-to-back weekend volume tailored for technical 80km mountain prep. Reason: Builds weekly base mileage toward the athlete's 136 km baseline while respecting the 30% single-run cap. Benefit: Trains muscular endurance in stabilizing hip complexes and enhances long-duration fat utilization efficiency. Warning: Do not race the uphills; drop to a rhythmic power-hike immediately if heart rate breaches 133 bpm.

workouts.title: Mountain Specific Long Run & Technical Vert
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 20 min easy trail jog @ 5:15/km, Zone 1 → 125 min mountain trail running and sustained power-hiking @ 4:45/km average movement pace, Zone 2 → Cool down 20 min slow trail jog @ 5:20/km, Zone 1. Overall: The primary long run of the week, structured to build specific downhill eccentric tolerance and uphill hiking stamina for an extreme vert mountain race. Utilizes poles and technical terrain to replicate the target event's steep demands. Capped appropriately within weekly load limits to ensure progressive adaptation without systemic breakdown. Reason: Core weekly cornerstone run placed on Sunday to simulate race-specific vertical volume and mountain fatigue resistance. Benefit: Drives structural tendon resilience, eccentric quad conditioning, gut tolerance at race fueling rates, and deep aerobic stamina. Warning: Descend with light, quick steps rather than heavy heel-striking to minimize joint impact forces; keep effort strictly conversational.

workouts.title: Easy Run + Hill Sprints
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min chạy nhẹ nhàng Zone 1-2 → 35 min chạy ổn định Zone 2 trên địa hình dốc nhẹ → 6 x 10s Hill Sprints dốc 12-15% dốc đứng toàn lực, 3 min đi bộ thả lỏng hồi phục hoàn toàn giữa mỗi rep → Cool down 10 min chạy chậm thả lỏng về Zone 1. Overall: Buổi chạy nền tảng aerobic kết hợp kích hoạt thần kinh cơ bắp đầu tiên của block. Bạn sẽ chạy tích lũy bền vững dưới ngưỡng hiếu khí AeT và đánh thức các sợi cơ co rút nhanh qua các cú bứt tốc dốc ngắn. Reason: Mở màn chu kỳ huấn luyện bằng việc kích thích hệ thần kinh trung ương và tuần hoàn mà không tích tụ acid lactic hay gây mệt mỏi toàn thân. Benefit: Tăng mật độ mao mạch, củng cố khả năng tuyển mộ sợi cơ FTa mà không ảnh hưởng tới nền tảng aerobic. Warning: Hill Sprints đòi hỏi nỗ lực bộc phát tối đa nhưng phải dừng ngay nếu thấy căng cứng bất thường ở gân gót hoặc bắp chân.

workouts.title: Long Run Aerobic Base
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 10 min chạy khởi động chậm rãi Zone 1 → 55 min chạy liên tục Zone 2 kiểm soát chặt chẽ HR dưới 158 bpm trên đường dốc thoai thoải → Cool down 10 min đi bộ và thả lỏng cơ bắp. Overall: Buổi Long Run mở đầu cuối tuần thiết lập sức bền hiếu khí cơ sở. Giữ nhịp thở đàm thoại đều đặn và bước chạy nhịp nhàng suốt hành trình. Reason: Tôn trọng trần chịu đựng lịch sử gần đây của bạn trong khi kích hoạt quá trình oxy hóa chất béo cho cự ly 50K sắp tới. Benefit: Tăng sinh ty thể, tối ưu hóa khả năng sử dụng chất béo làm nguồn nhiên liệu chính và củng cố độ bền dây chằng. Warning: Tuyệt đối không để nhịp tim vượt qua ngưỡng AeT 158 bpm ở các đoạn dốc; chủ động chuyển sang đi bộ nhanh nếu HR tăng cao.

workouts.title: Aerobic Base Run & Neuromuscular Strides
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy continuous running @ 5:44 /km → 40 min steady aerobic running @ 5:25 /km → 5 x 20s relaxed flat strides with 40s walk recovery (5 min) → Cool down 5 min easy jogging @ 6:00 /km. Overall: Smooth conversational base volume to open the training week followed by neuromuscular strides. Maintains running economy and recruits high-threshold motor units without metabolic fatigue. Reason: Establishes consistency right after missed sessions in week 1 while respecting historical ceiling limits. Benefit: Stimulates mitochondrial development, capillary density, and neuromuscular elasticity. Warning: Keep the strides relaxed and snappy; avoid sprinting all-out or straining hamstrings.

workouts.title: Aerobic Foundation & Bodyweight Circuit
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy running @ 5:45 /km → 35 min steady Zone 2 run @ 5:32 /km → Bodyweight Squats: 3x10, 90s rest → Walking Lunges: 3x10 each leg, 90s rest → Eccentric Calf Raises: 3x12 each leg, 60s rest → Single-Leg Glute Bridges: 3x10 each leg, 60s rest → Cool down 5 min mobility and stretching. Overall: Combined aerobic durability run and non-weighted functional strength work. Builds foundational leg resilience and stability without requiring gym equipment. Reason: Mountain ultramarathon preparation requires joint integrity and eccentric tolerance built early in the base period. Benefit: Enhances hip stability, patellar tendon durability, and running posture under mild fatigue. Warning: Maintain flawless form on bodyweight squats and lunges; stop immediately if knee tracking collapses inward.

workouts.title: Scheduled Rest Day
workouts.description: Process: Full rest day with zero structured physical training. Overall: Dedicated recovery day to allow systemic restoration and cellular adaptation. Essential for resetting glycogen stores and reducing autonomic nervous system strain. Reason: Wedged between initial aerobic loading and specific hill sprint work to guarantee structural recovery. Benefit: Promotes glycogen replenishment, hormonal normalization, and soft-tissue remodeling. Warning: Avoid strenuous physical chores or supplementary cross-training; honor complete physical rest.

workouts.title: Zone 2 Aerobic Run & Steep Hill Sprints
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 15 min progressive aerobic jog @ 5:44 /km → 26 min steady Zone 2 base run @ 5:25 /km → 8 x 10s maximal steep hill sprints on 12-15% grade, 170s full walking/standing recovery after each rep (24 min) → Cool down 5 min easy jog @ 6:00 /km. Overall: Aerobic maintenance run coupled with short, steep uphill sprints. Develops maximal neuromuscular recruitment without accumulating glycolytic cardiovascular fatigue. Reason: In the Uphill Athlete methodology, hill sprints build running economy and power independently of cardiac strain. Benefit: Recruits fast-twitch Type IIx motor units, strengthens Achilles and patellar tendons, and expands stride power. Warning: Maintain full standing or slow walking recovery between hill sprints; do not rush reps before ATP stores replenish fully.

workouts.title: Aerobic Recovery & Trail Mobility Run
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 10 min very easy jog @ 6:20 /km → 40 min gentle Zone 1 recovery run on flat-to-rolling trail @ 6:02 /km → Cool down 5 min walking mobility drills. Overall: Low-intensity recovery session aimed at flushing the legs and absorbing weekly aerobic volume. Strictly controlled to keep heart rate well below AeT. Reason: Provides active recovery before the weekend endurance block without placing stress on the endocrine system. Benefit: Increases capillary flushing, enhances fat oxidation, and accelerates clearance of cellular waste. Warning: Strictly obey the upper ceiling of Zone 1; walk any short steep rises to keep heart rate below 140 bpm.

workouts.title: Aerobic Base Volume & Rhythm Run
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy jog @ 5:45 /km → 55 min continuous steady aerobic running in mid Zone 2 @ 5:25 /km → Cool down 5 min walking and gentle mobility. Overall: Sustained aerobic volume run on rolling mixed terrain. Solidifies foundational aerobic capacity while prepping lower extremities for Sunday's longer outing. Reason: Accumulates weekly mileage in alignment with the athlete's 71 km volume baseline without exceeding physiological ceilings. Benefit: Enhances cardiac stroke volume, increases intramuscular glycogen storage capacity, and strengthens connective tissues. Warning: Monitor cadence on undulating terrain; avoid bounding on small descents to protect quadriceps.

workouts.title: Hilly Aerobic Long Run
workouts.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy jog @ 6:00 /km → 65 min steady mountain trail aerobic running in Zone 2 with power hiking on steep gradients @ 5:35 /km → Cool down 5 min walking and lower body mobility. Overall: Key weekend long run prioritizing continuous time on feet over hilly terrain. Serves as the cornerstone aerobic session while strictly honoring volume distribution caps. Reason: Expands structural endurance and introduces vertical climbing relevant to the 2700m D+ race profile. Benefit: Increases mitochondrial density in slow-twitch fibers, strengthens foot and ankle stabilisers, and improves fat utilization. Warning: Walk all steep uphills to prevent heart rate from drifting past AnT into Zone 4; descend with light, quick steps.
